plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes crowded with fragrant violet-blue flowers. Fields hum with bees, and the scent drifts for miles on warm summer air.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer, peaking from late June through July
plants.location: Provence, France, and the wider Mediterranean and temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. The Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Large, elegant blooms rise on tall stalks above round, water-repellent leaves. They open at dawn and look luminous over still summer ponds.
plants.location: Ponds and wetlands across Asia, including China, Japan and India, and in botanical gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic surface texture that sheds water and dirt, a effect scientists call the 'lotus effect' and have copied in self-cleaning materials.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like blooms with drooping rose-purple petals surround a spiky, copper-orange central cone. Butterflies and goldfinches flock to them in sunny meadows and gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early autumn, with strong flowering in July
plants.location: Eastern and central United States prairies and open woodlands, and gardens across North America
plants.funFact: The name Echinacea comes from the Greek 'echinos', meaning hedgehog, a nod to the prickly central cone.
